mvDailyStats.description:
Single row from ai_ecommerce.mv_daily_stats materialized analytics view. Represents platform-wide aggregation of daily sales, orders, logins, signups, and reviews for a single calendar day. Used as the atomic entity in analytics dashboards, statistical charting, reporting/reconciliation, and AI/ML input sets.

Denormalization is permitted here for performance (each field is an aggregate snapshot for the day).

id.description: Unique ID for stats row; UUID of the analytics view entry.

stat_date.description: Date for this record, format 'YYYY-MM-DD' (ISO) as string—key for daily analytics.

order_count.description: Total number of orders on this date.

login_count.description: Number of distinct logins (unique users) on this day.

signups_count.description: Aggregate users registered on this date.

review_count.description: Number of reviews written on this date.

stat_date.description:
The ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) representing the day for which the statistics are recorded. Used as the primary reference date for daily aggregation in analytics dashboards and reporting tools.

Should follow the ISO 8601 standard and match business regional settings. Examples: '2025-07-01', '2024-12-31'.

order_count.description:
The number of orders placed on the given stat_date. Aggregated from order data for reporting, KPI dashboards, and trend analytics.

Must be a non-negative integer. For example: 100.

revenue_amount.description:
The total revenue (sum of order amounts) for the day. Used in financial reporting, analytics, and trend monitoring.

Represents the sum in the platform's base currency (usually KRW, USD, etc.). Should match double-precision floating-point format. Examples: 1250000.75.

login_count.description:
Total unique user logins registered on the specific stat_date. Supports platform engagement and analytics use cases.

Must be non-negative. Example: 250.

signups_count.description:
The number of new account registrations that occurred on the stat_date. Supports growth, onboarding, and user acquisition metrics for analytics and admin dashboards.

Should be a non-negative integer (e.g., 20).

review_count.description:
Number of new product reviews posted on the stat_date. Used for engagement analytics and platform health reporting.

Should be non-negative. For example: 10.

mvDailyStats.ICreate.description: Creation structure for mvDailyStats, representing a day's aggregated analytics. Must include all fields for atomic, non-aggregated reporting. Derived from Prisma schema mv_daily_stats table and described for compliance/audit in analytics reporting. All fields are atomic and required.

stat_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the stats row. See mvDailyStats.ICreate for description.

order_count.description: Updated order count for this day. See mvDailyStats.ICreate for description.

revenue_amount.description: Updated revenue for this day. See mvDailyStats.ICreate for description.

login_count.description: Updated login count for this day. See mvDailyStats.ICreate for description.

signups_count.description: Updated signups count for this day. See mvDailyStats.ICreate for description.

review_count.description: Updated review count for this day. See mvDailyStats.ICreate for description.

mvDailyStats.IUpdate.description: Update structure for mvDailyStats. Used for entire row replacement as described in PUT endpoint documentation. All fields are required to ensure the materialized view row is completely replaced. Descriptions are as in mvDailyStats.ICreate.

stat_period.description:
The time period granularity for the trending analysis. Typically values: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'. Enables filtering/searching by aggregation level in dashboards or analytics UIs.

Business logic expects strict enumeration in implementations.

stat_date.description:
The ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the trending statistic group. Enables filtering and analytics queries by date window. Follows ISO 8601.

Examples: '2025-07-16', '2025-07-01'.

trend_rank.description:
The minimum or exact rank value for trend filtering (e.g., top 5, 10, etc). Used in analytics to order/filter trending product results.

Should be positive integer if used.

product_id.description: Unique product identifier (UUID format) to filter trending stats for a specific product. Enables focused analytics on a single product's trending performance.

mvTrendingProducts.IRequest.description: Request/filtering parameters for listing/searching mvTrendingProducts analytics records. Used by PATCH endpoint for dashboard analytics, top-product feeds, or AI-powered recommendation systems. Properties correspond to analytics filtering use cases as described in the ERD and endpoint specs.

data.description:
Array of mvTrendingProducts analytic records matching the query/filter criteria.

Each item contains all atomic analytics information for a product/stat period/stat date combination.

current.description:
Current page number for paginated result. Used in conjunction with limit and total counts for UI and API navigation.

Zero or one-based depending on API design.

limit.description:
Number of records per page (page size). Default can be 100; should match request or system policy.

Used by UI and scripts for batch processing.

records.description:
Total records found for query. Used for pagination controls in APIs and UIs.

Always non-negative integer.

pages.description: Total pages of results available for current query and pagination size. Calculated by records and limit.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata following IPage.IPagination structure: current, limit, records, pages.

IPageMvTrendingProducts.description: Paginated result set for mvTrendingProducts listing/search operations. Includes both array of analytics records and pagination metadata following IPage<I> interface as described in the AI E-Commerce documentation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the trending product analytics record. Used as PK for the materialized view row as per ERD.

product_id.description:
Reference to the ai_ecommerce_product row for which the trending analytics data is recorded. Required for joining and analytics reporting.

Must match product PK in product catalog.

stat_period.description:
Denotes time aggregation period for trending analytics (e.g., 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'). Value is typically used as an enum for period grouping.

Used for dashboard, recommendation, and analytics granularity.

stat_date.description:
The ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the trending product analytics interval. Used for grouping and time-based reporting.

Follows ISO 8601 business conventions.

trend_rank.description: Trending rank for this product in the specified period/date. Lower values indicate higher rank (e.g., 1 = top trend, 2, ...).

sales_count.description: Total count of sales for this product in the analytical window (stat_period/stat_date). Used for trending calculation and analytics dashboards.

views_count.description: Total views of the product in the given stat_period/stat_date. Used for popularity scoring and AI recommendation algorithms.

composite_score.description:
Business-configured composite score for trending products, calculated using sales, views, reviews, and additional analytics fields. Used to order/rank trending products/analytics.

Should reflect normalized or weighted algorithm scoring.

mvTrendingProducts.description: Materialized view record for trending products analytics. Contains all atomic, normalized analytics properties including rank, sales, views, and business composite score. Derived directly from Prisma schema ai_ecommerce_mv_trending_products and ERD specifications.

product_id.description: UUID reference to the product being ranked in this trending analytics window. Must correspond to PK in ai_ecommerce_product.

stat_period.description:
Period aggregation for trending analytics (enum: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'). Required for analytics aggregation/grouping.

Business rules expect system-enforced content.

stat_date.description: Date string (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD) representing the window for trending analytics. Used for filtering, UI display, and analytics grouping.

trend_rank.description:
Rank of this product for this period/date combination. Lower means higher trending position (1 = top trending).

Must be a positive integer.

sales_count.description:
Total number of times the product was sold in this stat period/date. Used in analytics for trend scoring.

Non-negative integer; required for full analytics row.

views_count.description:
Total number of times this product was viewed in the stat window. Used in composite scoring, analytics dashboards, and AI ranking.

Must be non-negative integer.

composite_score.description:
Composite (algorithmic) score used in trend ranking and AI/ML models. Calculated from sales, views, and engagement stats as per business rule.

Should match normalized or weighted scoring as described in algorithm documentation.

mvTrendingProducts.ICreate.description: Create structure for new analytics record in mvTrendingProducts (materialized view). All properties are required for atomic reporting, derived from ERD Prisma schema commented explanations.

product_id.description: UUID reference for the product to update trending stats for.

stat_date.description: ISO 8601 date string for stats window.

trend_rank.description: Updated trending rank for product/stat period/stat date.

sales_count.description: Updated total sales for trending row.

views_count.description: Updated total view count for the product window.

composite_score.description: Updated composite score for AI/analytics ranking/scoring.

mvTrendingProducts.IUpdate.description: Update structure for mvTrendingProducts: full replacement of analytics row for a trending product, stat period, and window. All atomic fields required. Used with PUT endpoint, descriptions as in ICreate.

authorization.name: customer
authorization.description: Individual users who can browse products, place orders, manage favorites, write reviews/inquiries, and access personalized features after authenticating via API. Customers may be members, guests, or external platform users.

authorization.name: seller
authorization.description: Authenticated business users who can list, manage, and fulfill products, view analytics, issue coupons, and respond to inquiries or reviews. Sellers manage their product catalogs and order workflow via API.

authorization.name: administrator
authorization.description: Platform-wide managers with permissions for system configuration, seller onboarding, channel management, marketing tools, and regulatory/audit modules. Administrators can access all system APIs for operational and analytic purposes.

reason: Step to the interface designing after DB schema generation

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can retrieve a paginated and filterable list of sellers. Test with various valid filter and pagination parameters (such as status, search by name, offset/limit), ensure that only allowed fields are included in responses, and confirm sorting and paging metadata accuracy. Edge cases: empty result for over-restrictive filters, and boundary paging (e.g., last page with less than pageSize results). Also, attempt a request with an invalid or malformed filter (e.g., bad status value) and confirm an appropriate error is returned.

Attempt to list sellers with a user lacking administrator privileges (e.g., customer, unauthenticated). Confirm that access is denied with a clear authorization error, ensuring privileged access is enforced and logged for compliance.

Retrieve seller detail using a valid seller id as administrator and confirm all permitted data (UUID, profile linkage, and status) is returned. Also, attempt to fetch with an invalid UUID format or non-existent id, expecting a descriptive not found or validation error. Edge cases: Try to view a soft-deleted seller and confirm the API indicates their deleted state.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid seller to guarantee a retrievable id for detail fetch.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new seller with valid, unique profile linkage and required onboarding fields using administrator privileges. Confirm that the response returns the correct seller record. Negative case: Attempt creation using a profile id already associated with another seller (to trigger uniqueness violation), or provide missing/invalid fields to validate constraint and error handling. Ensure all entity relationships are enforced and errors are properly described.

dependencies.purpose: Create a unique user profile to use as the profile_id for valid seller creation.

scenario.draft: Update fields of an existing seller as administrator and verify all permitted fields can be changed successfully (e.g., business metadata). Confirm audit fields are updated (updated_at). Test forbidden updates: attempt to change immutable fields (such as primary profile linkage or PK), expect an error and no change in the DB. Also, try to update a soft-deleted seller and confirm a failure response. Negative case: Attempt update by a user lacking admin privileges and confirm permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller to update with controlled initial conditions.

scenario.draft: Soft-delete a seller as an administrator and verify the deleted_at field is set. Afterwards, re-fetch the seller to confirm its soft-deleted state. Negative cases: Try to delete a non-existent seller (expect not found error), and attempt to delete an already-deleted seller again (expect an appropriate error indicating the record is already deleted). Attempt delete with insufficient privileges (non-admin) and ensure access control is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller to be deleted in the test, ensuring a valid id is available.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of user audit logs as both a regular user and administrator. Include scenarios where filters are valid and result in matches, as well as where filters are overly restrictive and result in zero results. Validate that permissions ensure a regular user sees only their own logs, while an administrator can see any log. Ensure that search by profile ID, event type, and date range works as expected. Trigger errors by submitting malformed filters or excessive page sizes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile needed to trigger audit events and for filter criteria.
Create multiple audit log records to populate the audit log entry table and verify retrieval accuracy.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single user audit log detail by ID as both an owner (user whose profile matches the audit log) and as an administrator. Cover scenarios where the audit log exists and is accessible, where the ID is valid but does not exist, and where the ID is not a valid UUID. Validate that access is forbidden for users who do not own the log or lack administrative rights. Ensure that deleted entries return the appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profiles for test users and admin roles.
Insert audit log records for the user profiles to supply valid log IDs for retrieval.
Delete a log to test retrieval of a deleted record.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a user audit log record for both valid and invalid scenarios. Successful case: normal user creates a log for their own profile, admin creates a log for any profile. Failure cases: attempt to create a log for someone else's profile as a non-admin, input missing required fields, or providing a non-existent profile ID. Validate that audit log entries are immutable after creation and check that all events are written in compliance with business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profiles—both for the requestor and for target profiles involved in audit logs.

scenario.draft: Test updating a user audit log as both the record owner (where permitted by policy) and an administrator. Validate that only permitted fields (typically metadata or rationale under compliance scenario) can be updated; attempts to update immutable fields (profile_id, event_type, etc.) or logs not eligible for edits (per compliance/immutability rules) should result in an error. Try updating both existing and non-existent audit logs, as well as logs that have been soft-deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profiles for log creation and permission tests.
Insert user audit logs to test updates on existing records.
Delete a user audit log for update scenario on soft-deleted records.

scenario.draft: Test the soft-delete of a user audit log by its owner (where allowed) and by admin, ensuring only permitted actors may perform the deletion. Cover error scenarios including attempts to delete logs that are already deleted, non-existent IDs, or deletion by unauthorized users. Validate that deletion state is correctly represented and that all deletion attempts are recorded in compliance log tables.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profiles to test owner and admin delete flows.
Insert logs for deletion scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test that listing/searching payments using PATCH /ai_ecommerce/payments applies pagination, filtering, and search options correctly. Covers filtering by status, date, provider, and customer/order reference fields (where permitted by role). Include scenarios for large-page handling, invalid filters (e.g., unsupported status or malformed date), and permission enforcement (e.g., only finance/admin/seller may access all payments, regular user receives permission error). Include scenario for requesting results with no matches (returns an empty list but valid pagination metadata). Verify proper error is returned on ill-formed request body or excessive page sizes violating service limits.

Test retrieval of a single payment record by valid payment ID as permitted user. Covers: (a) successful fetch by owner/admin, (b) error if payment does not exist (404), (c) forbidden if user lacks privilege to view another's payments, and (d) appropriate masking of sensitive fields as dictated by business role. Cover scenario for attempting to fetch a deleted or soft-deleted payment (returns proper error/status).

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid payment record for use in the fetch test.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new payment record with valid fields: successful insert returns the created object with all required details populated. Test constraint handling for uniqueness violations (e.g., duplicate payment_reference or re-creation of already settled payment), mandatory field omission, invalid order/payment_reference formats, and value checking (e.g., negative amount, invalid currency code). Try creating a payment for a non-existent order reference (should return error). Verify only allowed actors (admin/customer) can create a payment.

Verify updating an existing payment as a privileged actor. Test transition of payment status from 'pending' to 'completed', update of metadata (e.g., method or provider field), and ensure that mutation of immutable payments (e.g., settled/canceled) is rejected. Cover error paths for permission errors, non-existent payment ID, or forbidden changes to locked fields (such as amount or reference after settlement). Verify all changes trigger audit logging, and updates affect only permitted fields per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment record for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test deleting (removing) a payment by ID. Scenarios: (a) successful deletion of a valid, eligible payment by a privileged user, (b) error if attempting to delete a payment in settled/non-deletable state, (c) forbidden if deleting someone else's payment without permission, and (d) error code if deleting a non-existent record. Ensure all delete actions are logged for audit/compliance and system state after removal is as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment record to be deleted in the test. If needed, also test deleting payments in different business states, potentially requiring separate creation logic.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of seller business profiles. As an administrator, submit a request containing business name, registration number, and pagination parameters. Ensure the response contains only non-deleted entries, matching the filters, and proper pagination metadata. Also, include a scenario where filters yield no results. Validate permission controls prevent unauthorized access and properly handle malformed request bodies.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller accounts to ensure there are business profiles present for filtering and listing. Each created seller needs to be associated with a business profile.
Create at least two business profiles linked to different sellers to provide varied filterable data.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the details of a seller business profile by its UUID. First, create a seller and the corresponding business profile. Attempt to fetch the business profile with the correct ID as both admin and seller (owner). Validate that the full detail is returned. Next, attempt to access with an invalid or non-existent UUID and verify a not found error is returned. Also, ensure proper handling and error response when accessing a soft-deleted profile.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller so a business profile can be created and referenced.
Create a business profile linked to the seller, necessary for valid fetch operations.

scenario.draft: Test creating a seller business profile with all required fields as an admin or seller. Ensure the resulting entity is correctly persisted and returned. Attempt to create another profile for the same seller (should fail uniqueness constraint). Also try to create with missing mandatory fields and with duplicate business registration number (should fail with appropriate validation errors). Check permission controls: only admins or sellers acting on their own account can create profiles.

dependencies.purpose: Establish sellers to link with the new business profiles. Required for valid foreign key references in the creation process.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing seller business profile by its UUID. First, create a seller and associated business profile. As an authorized admin or seller, update only allowed fields (e.g., contact info, business name). Attempt to update with a registration number that already exists for another profile to trigger uniqueness violation. Also, attempt changing immutable fields (e.g., seller_id, deleted_at) or updating a soft-deleted profile and verify that appropriate error responses or blocks are enforced. Unauthorized role attempts should return forbidden errors.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a valid seller to own the business profile.
Create the business profile to be updated in tests.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a seller business profile by UUID as an authorized admin or owning seller. Ensure the deleted_at field is set and the entity is not returned in standard queries afterward. Attempt to delete a profile already soft-deleted and verify an error or appropriate duplicate-delete indication. Also, ensure that only authorized actors can soft-delete, and that referenced onboarding or audit logs remain intact for compliance. Attempt to delete a non-existent profile to receive a proper not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller to which a business profile can be linked.
Create the business profile intended for deletion in testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a filtered, paginated list of replies based on different targeting associations (comment, thread, inquiry, review). Scenario covers: (1) creating an inquiry as a customer, adding a top-level comment, then posting one or more replies to that comment as an admin or seller; (2) verifying replies are listed when filtering by the parent comment id; (3) testing reply search by actor (administrator_id or seller_id), by creation date range, and by keyword in reply body; (4) paginating the results. All replies for soft-deleted parents must not be returned unless requested. If filtering parameters are malformed or user lacks permission, expect robust error responses. Also, verify that only authorized actors can access system-wide reply list.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new inquiry as context for posting subsequent comments and replies.
Add a comment to the inquiry to serve as the parent for replies.
Create one or more replies associated with the initial comment or directly with the inquiry/thread/review, as relevant.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single reply by its UUID. (1) Create an administrator or seller actor, a forum thread or inquiry, a comment, and a corresponding reply on that comment. (2) Get the reply by its id and verify that all fields are present and correct, matching the creation data. (3) Attempt to fetch a reply with a non-existent UUID and expect a 404 error. (4) Attempt to access a reply the user is not authorized to see (e.g., another seller's reply as a non-admin) and verify a 403/permission error if applicable. (5) If the reply is soft-deleted, verify default logic hides it unless sufficient privilege is present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base comment to serve as parent for the reply.
Create a reply to associate with the base comment.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a reply to a comment (forum, inquiry, review) using either seller or administrator actor. Steps: (1) Create a comment as the base, (2) Post a reply as an administrator to that comment, verify the reply is linked properly, (3) Post a reply as a seller to another relevant entity; (4) Validate creation fails if no actor or target ID is supplied, or if both seller_id and administrator_id are missing. (5) Attempt to reply to a deleted or non-existent parent and verify an error is returned. (6) Confirm audit trails are created for reply creation events.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to which a reply will be added.

scenario.draft: Test that creating a reply with multiple non-null target references (e.g., both comment_id and review_id) is rejected as invalid, enforcing atomic association per business rule.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment for reply association.

scenario.draft: Test updating a reply's body text by the original author (admin or seller). Steps: (1) Post a new reply; (2) Update the reply with revised content as the author; (3) Confirm the modification succeeds and updated data is reflected; (4) Attempt the update as a different user and verify access is denied; (5) Attempt update on a reply that has been soft-deleted and expect error or denial according to system rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base comment and its reply, as context for update actions.
Create a reply to update.

scenario.draft: Test updating a reply to change fields which are not allowed (such as switching the association to a different comment, thread, or review after creation). Scenario must check that attempting to change association fields is rejected with a clear error, and that only permissible (such as body) fields may be changed post-creation. Also validate that the update payload is robustly validated for required/mutable properties.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment for reply association.
Create a reply to update.

scenario.draft: Test soft deletion of a reply by its owner (admin/seller) or a privileged admin. Steps: (1) Post a reply by a seller and by an admin. (2) Owner initiates deletion and confirms the reply is marked deleted_at (not hard deleted); (3) Admin initiates the same for another actor's reply and expects success; (4) Attempt to delete a reply as an unauthorized user and expect permission denied error; (5) Try deleting a reply already soft-deleted and validate idempotent/status-appropriate response.

dependencies.purpose: Create comment and associated replies for deletion scenarios.
Create different replies to be deleted under varying roles/contexts.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of personalization config records. Cover scenarios with no filters (all records), filters by admin_id, customer_id, config_key, and date ranges. Test pagination (limit/offset), sorting, and combinations of filters. Verify only permitted users can access sensitive configs, and that the system handles empty results as well as non-existent filter values. Test handling of malformed queries (invalid datatypes) and role-based access denial (e.g., normal user tries to list all configs).

Test fetching the full detail of a personalization config record by its ID. First, create an admin and a customer with appropriate roles. Then, create at least one config for each. Test retrieval by an authorized admin, an authorized customer (for their own config), and by an unauthorized role or unrelated user. Check correct error codes for non-existent IDs and for forbidden access. Verify the response does not leak sensitive data across roles. Attempt access to a deleted or soft-deleted config (if such logic exists) and confirm proper error/visibility state.

dependencies.purpose: Create a personalization config as data setup to test fetching behavior.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a personalization config with all required fields. Use admin or privileged customer as the creator. Validate that config_key uniqueness is enforced for time/customers. Attempt creation with duplicate config_key, missing required fields, or invalid data types to ensure validation errors are returned. Verify creation fails for unauthorized roles. On success, check that the returned object matches input and audit rules are honored.

Test updating a personalization config by its ID. Set up with a previously created config (using POST). Attempt updates to mutable fields such as config_value, applied_at, and admin/customer assignment. Attempt to update immutable fields (if any exist, such as id or created_at) and ensure errors are returned. Cover role-based permissions: authorized admin, the owning customer, and a non-privileged user. Try updating a non-existent config ID and confirm correct not-found error. Validate audit logging or history is maintained if relevant.

dependencies.purpose: Personalization config must exist before it can be updated.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a personalization config by ID. Create a config as setup, and then attempt deletion as an authorized admin and as an unauthorized customer. Verify soft/hard delete policy as per system (typically soft delete for audit). Try to delete a config that is already deleted or does not exist and verify not-found or idempotent result. Ensure audit trails are updated upon deletion when required by compliance. Validate that the deleted config cannot be accessed after removal.

dependencies.purpose: Config must already exist to test deletion flows.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a list of cart items with different filtering and pagination options. Scenario includes searching by cart ID, customer ID, SKU ID, and applying limit/offset for pagination. Also test behavior when applying invalid filter fields, excessive page sizes, or malformed request bodies. Verify results for authorized customer and administrator roles, confirming unauthorized/falsely scoped queries are rejected or return only items belonging to the actor.

dependencies.purpose: Create a shopping cart for the customer to receive a valid cart ID for querying cart items.
Add at least two items to the cart with different SKU IDs so filters and pagination may be exercised.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a cart item with a valid ID belonging to the customer to confirm correct detail retrieval. Test error response when attempting to fetch a non-existent cart item ID or one not owned by the requester. Confirm forbidden error if another user tries to fetch a cart item in a cart they don't own, and verify not found scenario for invalid or deleted IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a cart for the customer so a cart item can be assigned.
Create a cart item to get a valid ID for detail retrieval test.

scenario.draft: Test adding a SKU to an existing cart. First, ensure the cart and SKU exist. Test success by adding a valid SKU with a permitted quantity. Test business rule violation—try to add a duplicate SKU to the same cart (which should increment quantity instead of creating a new item if design requires), invalid SKU/cart IDs, and invalid (zero or negative) quantities. Validate that unauthorized users can't add to another user's cart.

dependencies.purpose: Create a cart for the customer to receive a cart ID for item addition.
Generate a new product to obtain a valid product and seller context for SKU creation.
Create a SKU for the product to use as SKU_ID in cart item creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating the quantity of an existing cart item by ID. First, prepare a cart item and update its quantity to a new valid value. Test boundary cases: set quantity to zero (which may be interpreted as removal or error), set to a negative number (should return a validation error). Attempt update for an item not owned by current user to confirm proper permission enforcement. Test updates after item has been deleted to confirm not found/locked error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer-owned cart to stage a cart item.
Create a product to be associated with the test SKU.
Generate a SKU for cart item creation.
Add a cart item that can then be updated by this test.

scenario.draft: Test deleting an existing cart item by its ID as the owning user. Expect success and confirmation of removal. Then, attempt to delete a non-existent cart item ID and a cart item not owned by the current user to verify proper error responses are returned for not found and forbidden cases. Verify repeated deletion behavior—attempt deleting the same item twice to confirm idempotency or error response on subsequent calls.

dependencies.purpose: Create a cart for associating the test cart item with a customer.
Create a product linked to a SKU.
Ensure a valid SKU for the cart item.
Create a cart item to perform delete tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of orders, filtered by order status and customer. The scenario should verify correct pagination metadata, correct filtering results, and that the returned orders only belong to the requesting customer (unless admin or seller role). Validation also includes that only authorized roles can use advanced search capabilities and that invalid filters (e.g., nonexistent status) return clear error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create several orders for at least two customers to set up a realistic test set. This ensures there are orders to filter and paginate.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a single order's detailed information by its ID, including all relevant metadata and relationships (customer, payment state, shipment, etc.). Also test requesting a non-existent order ID and expect a 404 error return. Validation is required for permission boundaries—customers may only get their own orders, while admin users can access any order. Edge case: attempt to access a deleted/cancelled order to verify business logic returns the appropriate error/visibility.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to obtain a valid order ID for positive test case.

scenario.draft: Test order creation by submitting a cart ID, shipping address, customer, and valid payment method. Verify business logic: an order is only created if the referenced cart and address are valid, the cart contains items, and inventory is sufficient. On success, a new order record should be returned. Test that only authenticated customers or authorized admins can perform this action. Dependency order: create a user profile, add cart, add items, and set user address.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user/customer profile for test order ownership and address.
Create a cart for the test customer.
Add at least one item (SKU) to the test cart.
Create a shipping address for the customer, used in the order creation request.

scenario.draft: Test that creating an order with an invalid, non-existent, or empty cart fails with a clear error describing the problem (e.g., invalid cart ID, cart without items, or cart belonging to a different customer). The error response should not expose sensitive data and should guide proper usage. Test scenarios: using a deleted/expired cart, an empty cart, or a cart owned by another user.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one customer profile for test ownership.
Create a cart for negative test scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test updating an order's status and shipping address via PUT by the rightful order owner or an admin user. The workflow includes order creation, then sending an update with new valid values for modifiable fields. The API must reject updates to non-modifiable fields and attempts by non-owners/non-admins. Verify that state transitions respect business rules (e.g., can't change status once delivered) and that changes are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to update, ensuring ownership is clear for positive and negative permission tests.
Create a secondary address to update the shipping address.

scenario.draft: Test failure cases: attempting to update a non-existent order (should return 404 error) and trying to update immutable fields or change status illegally (i.e., making a forbidden state transition). Ensure errors are descriptive and no data is changed. Scenarios include using a random UUID, updating as an unauthorized user, and attempting to edit after order is locked (e.g., after shipment or cancellation).

dependencies.purpose: Create an order for negative tests of update operations, covering valid but forbidden scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test that an order can be deleted (or soft-deleted, i.e., cancelled) by its owner or an admin user. Verify business logic: only open or eligible orders can be deleted, deletions are marked (not hard removed), associated data is not orphaned, and attempts to delete an already deleted/cancelled or ineligible order fail with a clear error. Ensure audit/log events are generated. Edge case: attempt delete by other users must fail permission check.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to test successful and failed delete scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to delete an order with a non-existent ID, expecting a 404 or relevant error. Validate that non-existent orders cannot be erroneously deleted and that the error message is clear and safe for the client.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of wallet transactions with various filters such as by transaction type, customer ID, date range, and sorting. This scenario should check that a customer and corresponding wallet exist and that the result contains only records that match the filter criteria. Also verifies correct pagination metadata and respects RBAC, ensuring only privileged users or wallet owners can see matching data. Edge cases: no results on overly strict filters, appropriate error if using invalid filter parameters, or insufficient permission.

dependencies.purpose: Create a wallet for customer so that there is at least one wallet to search for
Create a test user profile to associate with the wallet

scenario.draft: Test fetching details for a specific wallet transaction by ID. First, create a wallet and a valid wallet transaction, then retrieve it by its ID and verify that all expected fields match. Also test with a non-existent or invalid transaction ID and ensure the endpoint returns the appropriate not found or permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a wallet transaction to get a valid transaction ID
Ensure a wallet exists for transaction
Provide a user profile for wallet association

scenario.draft: Test creating a new wallet transaction with valid data, linking to an existing wallet, and verifying that the transaction is created as expected. Also test failure cases: creating a transaction with invalid wallet ID, negative change_amount (if not allowed), or with insufficient user privileges. Check that business rules such as transaction type validity and amount constraints are properly enforced and that errors returned are descriptive.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there is a wallet to associate with the new transaction.
Provide a user profile to link to the wallet.

scenario.draft: Test updating the details of an existing wallet transaction with correct privileges and valid update payload (e.g., correcting metadata or details_json). First, create a wallet and a transaction, then update allowed fields and verify changes. Also test forbidden updates when attempting to change immutable fields, or update locked/settled transactions. Edge cases: try update with non-existent transaction ID and expect a not found error, or attempt updates with insufficient privilege and check for access denial.

dependencies.purpose: Create a transaction to be updated.
Ensure the transaction is linked to a real wallet.
Create a user profile for wallet association.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a wallet transaction by its ID as an authorized user (admin or wallet owner), ensuring proper deletion when allowed. First, create a wallet transaction, delete it, and verify that reading it afterward reflects the deleted or not found status. Also, attempt to delete a transaction that is locked/settled and expect a compliance or immutability error. Try deleting a transaction as an unauthorized user and verify access is denied. Edge: deleting non-existent transaction should return a clear not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a wallet transaction to be deleted.
Link transaction to a valid wallet.
Create a customer profile as wallet owner.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of SKUs using various search and filter options. Start by creating multiple products and attach several SKUs to each, varying properties such as status, code, and price. Use the /ai_ecommerce/skus endpoint to filter SKUs by product, status, code patterns, and price range, and verify that the paginated result returns only SKUs matching the criteria. Confirm that requesting out-of-bounds or invalid pagination parameters (negative page, excessive size) returns a proper error. Depend on product and SKU creation endpoints for test setup.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple product entities to establish required parent products for test SKUs.
Create several SKUs with varying fields to test filtering, searching, and pagination features.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single SKU entity by its UUID. First, create a new SKU and fetch it by its generated ID, verifying all fields are returned accurately. Then, attempt to fetch SKUs using invalid UUID format and non-existent IDs, confirming that appropriate error responses (404 not found, validation error) are returned. Test access controls for restricted SKUs (if applicable by schema or business logic). Requires product and SKU creation as setup.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product record that can be associated with a new SKU.
Create a SKU so that a valid SKU ID is available for retrieval testing.

scenario.draft: Test SKU creation with a variety of valid and invalid payloads. First, create a product to attach the SKU to. Create a SKU using valid parameters (product_id, unique code, price, currency, is_active). Confirm that the SKU is created and returned as expected. Attempt to create a SKU with a duplicate code for the same product (should fail with unique constraint error), with missing required fields, with an invalid product_id (non-existent), and with negative or zero price. Check that each failure scenario returns a detailed validation or business logic error. Creation must be transactional, so verify no partial writes on error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product entity to be referenced by the SKU in creation tests.

scenario.draft: Test updating SKU fields (such as code, price, currency, is_active) via PUT. Start by creating a product, then a SKU for that product. Update allowed fields and verify changes are persisted and properly returned. Attempt to update with a code that already exists for the same product (unique constraint violation), try referencing a non-existent product in an update, and attempt to update immutable fields (if any defined by business logic, e.g., id). Also test updating with invalid values (negative price, invalid currency code). Ensure transactionality: either all valid updates are applied, or the system returns a clear error with no partial change.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product for associating with the SKU to be updated.
Create an initial SKU so valid SKU ID is available for update scenario.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a SKU record by ID. Create a product and a SKU, then delete the SKU and verify the deleted_at timestamp is set and the SKU becomes inactive. Attempt to delete a SKU that does not exist, and a SKU that is already deleted, confirming that appropriate error statuses are returned each time. If the system prevents deletion of SKUs in use (e.g., active orders), simulate this by associating the SKU with an order and confirm deletion is appropriately blocked. All delete actions should be audited or logged per business compliance rules. Verification includes dependency on related product and SKU creation, and potentially order creation endpoints if order linkage prevents deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to attach SKUs for deletion tests.
Create a SKU to test successful and unsuccessful deletion scenarios.
(Conditional) If business rules prevent deleting SKUs in use, create an order using this SKU to simulate locked state.

scenario.draft: Test the ability to list and filter media assets using various filter parameters such as owner type, media type, and soft-delete status. Start by seeding several media assets with distinct owners, types, and statuses via POST /ai_ecommerce/media. Then send a PATCH request with filter and pagination parameters. Verify that only the permitted user roles (administrator, seller) can access the endpoint, and that the response accurately reflects search criteria and pagination. Also check that soft-deleted records are excluded from standard queries unless explicitly requested.

dependencies.purpose: Seed a variety of media assets with different owners, types, and statuses to test filtering and pagination accurately.

scenario.draft: Test that unauthorized users (i.e., roles other than administrator or seller) cannot retrieve the media list. Attempt to call PATCH /ai_ecommerce/media as an unauthorized user and verify that access is denied with an appropriate error message and status code.

Test that the endpoint returns a clear and descriptive error when called with malformed or invalid filter parameters (e.g., nonsensical owner type, invalid pagination tokens). Ensure the system gracefully handles filter errors and provides informative feedback.

Test that an authorized user (administrator or the asset's owner seller) retrieves the correct metadata and details for a media asset. First, create a media asset and then use its id to request details. Check that the returned data matches the stored media metadata and access control rules are observed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new media asset so its id can be used for subsequent detail retrieval and permission validation.

scenario.draft: Attempt to access a media asset's details as an unauthorized/irrelevant user and verify that access is strictly denied, returning an appropriate error code/message.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new media asset to verify unauthorized access restrictions by attempting to fetch it as a non-owner/non-admin.

scenario.draft: Request details for a non-existent or soft-deleted media id and verify that the endpoint returns a proper not found or forbidden response. Ensure the error is clear and not ambiguous, and that deleted resources are not exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete an existing media asset prior to attempting its retrieval, ensuring the deleted state is honored for subsequent GET operations.

scenario.draft: Test the successful creation of a media asset when all required fields and valid metadata are provided. Verify that the returned response contains the full, correct media object including its UUID. Then use GET to ensure data persistence.

Attempt to create a media asset with missing required fields, invalid field formats, or disallowed values (such as empty URIs or invalid type). Confirm that the endpoint rejects the request with informative validation errors and does not create any media record.
Attempt to create a media asset as an unauthorized role (e.g., not an admin or seller) and verify that the action is blocked with a proper permission-denied response.

Test updating metadata fields (description, tags, language, etc.) for a media asset as the authorized owner (administrator/seller). First, create a media asset, then update its metadata. Verify the update persists as expected and audit trails are maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new media asset for updating and validation of update behavior.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a media asset as a user with no ownership or appropriate role and ensure the request is rejected with a clear permission error, leaving the data unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a media asset for which another user will attempt an unauthorized update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a non-existent or soft-deleted media record. Ensure the endpoint returns a not found or forbidden error and does not allow the update.

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete the media asset (or use random id) and then attempt the update, confirming proper error handling and data invariants.

scenario.draft: Test successful soft-delete of a media asset by an authorized owner (administrator/seller). First, create a media asset, then perform the delete operation. Verify the deleted media is no longer shown in standard searches and is flagged as deleted in detail view (if supported), and access attempts after deletion respond as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a media asset to be subsequently soft-deleted, enabling a full resource lifecycle test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a media asset as an unauthorized actor (not admin or owner seller) and ensure operation fails with a permission-denied response and audit log is updated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a media asset with ownership belonging to another account/user, to test unauthorized delete behavior.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a media record by a nonexistent or already deleted id and verify the endpoint returns a not found error, providing clear feedback and not affecting other records.

Test that an authenticated user retrieves their list of addresses filtered by profile_id and paginated. Verify the response contains only non-deleted addresses that belong to the requested profile, correct number of results, and pagination metadata. Ensure that addresses from other profiles or soft-deleted entries are not included. Edge case: request with empty page or over-limit page size returns appropriate errors or empty dataset.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile to associate addresses with and for filtering results.
Create multiple addresses for the given user profile to ensure pagination and filtering will have meaningful data.

scenario.draft: Verify that a user can retrieve details of an address they own and that is not soft-deleted. Confirm that the returned address matches the expected profile and address data, and does not expose content of deleted or unrelated addresses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile for the test user.
Create a user address associated with the profile to retrieve by ID.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve an address by a valid UUID that either does not exist or has been soft-deleted. Confirm that the response is an appropriate not-found error or deleted status, not the actual address data. Both non-existent and soft-deleted scenarios must be covered.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile for address association.
Create and then soft-delete a user address for negative test case.
Soft-delete the user address to simulate the deleted state for negative test.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new user address using only the minimum required fields. Verify that the address is recorded in the system, correctly linked to the user profile, and that required validations (region, address_type, is_default logic) pass. Response should return the new address object with all expected properties populated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile to assign as profile_id in the new address.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a user address with one or more required fields omitted (e.g., no profile_id or address_type). Confirm that the API returns a descriptive validation error and does not create the address in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile to attempt address creation (with incomplete payload).

scenario.draft: Test logic that prevents creating more than one default address (is_default=true) for the same profile and address type (e.g., delivery). After creating an initial default address for a profile, attempt to create another address with is_default=true of the same type and confirm that a business logic error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile for the scenario.
Create the first default address for a given type (e.g., delivery).

scenario.draft: Verify that a user can update allowed fields (such as address line, name, is_default) of their own address record. Confirm that validation is enforced and updated_at timestamp is changed. Response should include the updated address values.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profile for update scenario.
Create the initial address record to be updated.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a user address with invalid data, such as an empty required field or violating unique address-type constraints. Ensure validation errors are returned and no changes are made to the address record.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a profile for update-negative scenario.
Prepare an existing address for invalid updates.

scenario.draft: Try to update an address that either does not exist or has already been soft-deleted. Verify a not-found or appropriate business error, and ensure no record is affected.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profile for setup.
Create and then soft-delete the address to test update after deletion.
Soft-delete the address record to simulate update-after-delete.

scenario.draft: Test that a user can successfully soft-delete their own address that is not an active order address nor set as default. The deleted address should not appear in subsequent queries, and deleted_at should be set. Response should be 204 or similar confirmation.

dependencies.purpose: Create user profile for address deletion.
Create an address to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an address that is in use (e.g., referenced in an active order) or currently marked as the default delivery address for the user. Confirm that the API prevents deletion and returns the correct business error, and no deletion occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile for address in-use/delete scenario.
Create an address record set as default or link to order (dependency for in-use check).

scenario.draft: Test the ability to retrieve a paginated and filtered list of user profiles by specifying valid search parameters, such as nickname, email, and pagination options (page and size). The system should return a list of active, non-deleted profiles, matching the criteria, with correct paging metadata. This scenario validates core searching and listing functionality for customer service or admin users.

Attempt to search or paginate user profiles using invalid filter parameters, such as malformed email addresses, unsupported sort keys, negative page values, or excessive page sizes. The system should return clear validation errors for unsupported, malformed, or abusive request patterns. Ensures robust parameter validation and prevents resource abuse or server overload.

Create several active user profiles and soft-delete at least one. Then, perform a profile list/search request and verify no soft-deleted users are returned in the results, even if filters would otherwise match them. Ensures logical list filtering and privacy compliance by default.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple active user profiles in preparation for the test.
Soft-delete one of the previously created user profiles to set up an exclusion scenario for the list retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single user profile by supplying a valid existing profile ID. Confirm the returned data matches the created profile and includes only permitted fields with no sensitive PII. This validates both detail-fetch functionality and output field security.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile and obtain its ID to use in the retrieval scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to fetch a user profile using a well-formed but nonexistent UUID. The system should return a clear, well-structured error (e.g., 404 Not Found), demonstrating correct error handling for record lookups that do not exist.

Attempt to fetch the details of a user profile that has been soft-deleted. The system should return an error or empty response, as per business logic, and should not disclose details of deleted accounts. This tests privacy and compliance behavior for deleted resources.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile and soft-delete it before attempting to fetch it by ID.
Soft-delete the newly created profile for use in the error-checking scenario.

scenario.draft: Validate successful creation of a user profile when all required fields (nickname, email, communication consent, etc.) are provided and conform to uniqueness and business rules. The scenario asserts proper new profile creation in the system and verifies that sensitive fields are not leaked in the response.

Test profile creation failure when attempting to use an email that already exists in the system. First, create a user profile with a specific email, then attempt to create a second profile using the same email address. The system should return a conflict or validation error indicating email uniqueness is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial user profile to occupy the email address required for the duplicate constraint test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a user profile omitting one or more mandatory fields (such as nickname or email). Validate that the API rejects the input with a clear validation error, ensuring enforcement of required field constraints.

Attempt to create a user profile using an invalid email format (e.g., missing '@' sign or domain parts). Confirm the system rejects the request with a specific validation error related to email formatting rules.

Update a user profile by supplying valid new values for updatable fields such as nickname or communication preferences, but without changing the email to an already-in-use one. Verify that changes are persisted and returned in the response. Ensures the happy-path update scenario functions end-to-end.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile to be updated during the test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a user profile to change its email to another existing user's email address. Confirm the API returns a conflict or validation error, enforcing unique email restrictions.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first user profile to obtain an email address.
Create the second profile, which will then be updated to use the first one's email (should fail).

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a profile's email to an invalid format (e.g., missing '@' or domain). The system must reject the update with an explicit validation error, ensuring compliance with data format rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create the user profile to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a profile that has already been soft-deleted. The system should return an error and not allow modifications, ensuring compliance with deletion and audit rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile and soft-delete it for this error scenario.
Soft-delete the created user profile before attempting to update it.

scenario.draft: Soft-delete a user profile by its ID. After deletion, verify that the profile is marked as deleted (deleted_at set/not null), is no longer returned in list/search requests, and cannot be fetched by ID. Ensures full compliance with logical deletion business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile to be soft-deleted and validated during this scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a profile using a non-existent UUID. The operation should return a clear error (e.g., 404 Not Found), confirming safe error handling for delete operations.

Attempt to soft-delete a profile that is already soft-deleted. The system should return a clear, idempotent error or status message indicating the resource is already removed or ineligible for further deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user profile, then soft-delete it prior to performing the idempotent delete request.
Soft-delete the newly created user profile before re-attempting deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can retrieve a paginated, filtered list of loyalty tiers. The test should include scenarios where the list is filtered by name, minimum points, and order. Also check edge cases: (1) no results if a filter doesn't match any tier, (2) correct result when only one tier fits the filter, (3) pagination behavior when total results exceed page size, and (4) a request with invalid filter parameters that should return an appropriate error. Access control: verify that unauthorized non-administrators cannot retrieve the list or see tier information. All returned data must match the schema, and data not intended for the role should not be exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Loyalty tiers must exist to enable list and filtering test scenarios. Add several tiers with different names, point thresholds, and orders, as setup for pagination, filtering, and uniqueness tests.

scenario.draft: Test detailed retrieval of a single loyalty tier by its unique ID. Success case: admin requests an existing tier and receives all expected fields. Not found scenario: attempt to fetch a tier with a nonexistent or deleted ID and verify a proper 404 error. Access control: Ensure only admins can access detailed tier info, and other roles are denied. Schema and data privacy must be enforced for the role context.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one known loyalty tier to later fetch by ID and verify retrieval accuracy.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a loyalty tier, providing all required fields (name, minimum points, multiplier, sort order) as an administrator. Business rule: tier name must be unique. Validate failure when attempting to create another tier with the same name or order. Edge case: creation with minimum acceptable values, and creation with maximum constraints (such as a very large point threshold or multiplier). Confirm errors have clear messages and no tier is created on failure. After success, verify fields on the returned entity and confirm audit logging (if required).

Test updating an existing loyalty tier, changing editable fields as allowed (name, multiplier, minimum points, sort order). Verify a successful update as an administrator, and ensure the response accurately reflects the changes. Test failure when attempting to: (a) update a nonexistent tier (should error); (b) change a name or sort order to a value already in use by another tier (uniqueness violation); (c) provide invalid values for numeric fields (e.g., negative points, invalid multiplier).
