scenario.draft: Delete (erase) an existing personalization analytics event. Setup: create a new analytics record, delete it, and verify it is no longer retrievable by GET. Business value: Confirms support for compliance or legal deletion requests and maintains accurate event visibility.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new analytics event for targeted deletion test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a non-existent personalization analytics event. Verify the API returns an appropriate not found or compliance error. Business value: Ensures correct status signaling and system stability for requests against deleted or never-created events.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of payment integration providers. Scenario should verify: (1) All integrations are returned for admin with no filters, (2) Filtering by provider_name and is_active returns only matching records, (3) Pagination returns correct page/size and total count metadata, (4) Sorting by provider_name returns integrations in the expected order, (5) Searching for a nonexistent provider returns empty results, and (6) Attempts to use invalid filters or excessive page size are handled with proper error responses. Security rules dictate that only admin is allowed; test permission denials for non-admin users. Success requires records to match filter criteria, while errors should clearly indicate issues with request structure or authorization.

Verify that non-administrative or unauthorized roles cannot retrieve the list of payment integrations. Attempt access as non-admin user and confirm an appropriate forbidden/unauthorized error is returned. This test ensures security boundaries are enforced for sensitive payment configuration data.

Test retrieving payment integration configuration by valid and invalid id. Scenario steps: (1) As admin, create a payment integration so a valid id exists. (2) Retrieve the integration by its valid id and verify all metadata is correct. (3) Attempt retrieval with a randomly generated or unused id and verify a 404 Not Found error is returned. (4) Try with a malformed/non-UUID id and expect a 400 Bad Request or validation error. Also verify that sensitive info is returned only to authorized admin roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment integration so there is a valid id to retrieve for the success case.

scenario.draft: Verify forbidden access error when a non-admin user attempts to fetch payment integration configuration by id. Attempt to retrieve as an unauthorized or low-privilege user and confirm system rejects the request with appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment integration to provide an id for the test.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a payment integration by supplying all required fields (provider name, configuration_json, is_active). (1) As admin, create a new payment integration with valid data and ensure the integration is returned with all properties correctly set and is usable by subsequent GET operations. (2) Attempt to create another integration with the same provider_name, expecting a uniqueness-violation error response. (3) Try submitting a malformed configuration_json or missing required property, expecting a validation error.
Confirm business rules that non-admin users are not allowed to create payment integrations. Attempt to POST as a non-admin and expect an explicit error message about insufficient privileges.

Test updating an existing payment integration: (1) Successfully update fields such as configuration_json or is_active as admin, and verify all updates persist and metadata remains unchanged except intended fields. (2) Attempt to update a provider_name to collision with another integration and expect a uniqueness violation error. (3) Attempt to update with malformed configuration_json or invalid property, expecting validation error. (4) Test updating a nonexistent or already-deleted record to confirm proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more payment integrations to provide updatable ids and allow conflict testing.

scenario.draft: Validate that only admin users are allowed to update payment integrations; non-privileged actors must receive a forbidden/unauthorized response when attempting to PUT changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment integration whose id will be used in the update attempt.

scenario.draft: Test deletion (deactivation) of a payment integration by id. (1) As admin, ensure successful deletion returns confirmation and further use of the integration is not possible. (2) Attempt to delete the same id again, expecting a not found or already deactivated response. (3) Attempt to delete a nonexistent or malformed id and ensure system properly reports the error. (4) If the integration has active dependency (e.g., ongoing payments), verify the system blocks deletion and explains reason (business rule dependent).

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment integration to provide a valid id for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that only admins are permitted to delete payment integration configurations. Non-admin attempts must be met with a clear forbidden/unauthorized error. Attempts include both deleting integrations created by self and by others.

dependencies.purpose: Create a payment integration in order to supply an id for unauthorized deletion attempts.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of discount rules, using various combinations of filter parameters such as rule_type, creation date ranges, and description keyword search. Verify that the response contains only discount rules matching the filters, respects pagination limits, sorts as requested, and includes correct metadata (total count, pages, etc). Cover cases of empty results, excessive page requests, invalid filter structures, and permission errors (if any). Confirm that only authorized roles (administrator/operator) can access the endpoint and that unauthorized queries are rejected with appropriate error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Create several discount rules with different rule_type, descriptions, and dates to populate data for filter and pagination scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a discount rule by a valid ID and ensure that the correct details are returned according to the schema, including rule_type, description, and predicate_json. Also, perform negative testing by retrieving with a non-existent or invalid ID and confirm that the system returns a 404 Not Found error, as well as permission checks for unauthorized actors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discount rule and extract its ID for use in a valid detail fetch scenario.

scenario.draft: Test creating a discount rule with valid rule_type, description, and valid JSON predicate. Confirm that the rule is created successfully and the response matches the submitted data. Test business logic: attempt to create a duplicate rule (e.g., same combination of rule_type and logic if the business restricts duplication), invalid predicate_json, missing required fields, and unauthorized user attempts. Ensure errors are clear and no invalid records are created in these cases.

Test updating an existing discount rule's details (e.g., updating the description or changing the predicate_json) and ensure the response reflects the updated rule. Validate business constraints: updating to a duplicate rule_type/predicate combination (if restricted), trying to modify immutable fields, or submitting malformed JSON. Test negative paths: updating a non-existent rule (should error), and unauthorized role attempting update (should be rejected).

dependencies.purpose: Create a discount rule to have an updatable target for this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a discount rule by a valid ID and ensure the rule becomes inactive or is removed per business rules. Attempt to delete a rule which is currently referenced in an active coupon or promotion, expecting the operation to be blocked or to error as per referential integrity. Try deleting a non-existent or already deleted rule to check for proper error handling. Ensure permissions are enforced so only allowed actors (admins/operators) can perform deletions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discount rule to be deleted in the scenario.
Create a coupon referencing the discount rule to test referential deletion constraints.

scenario.draft: Test listing and searching abuse/violation reports with different filters (such as reporter, target type, status, date ranges, and keyword search) and pagination. Simulate both administrator and unauthorized user roles to verify that only authorized roles can access report lists. Check that queries with no results, malformed filters, or insufficient privileges return appropriate errors. Ensure paginated results supply correct metadata. Include edge cases like searching reports with special characters or very large page sizes to test system limits and defensive response.

dependencies.purpose: Create several abuse reports with varying properties so they can be searched and filtered by the test scenario.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the detailed information of a specific abuse report by ID. First, create a new report and successfully retrieve it by its ID, verifying all details are correct. Then attempt to fetch a report using a non-existent, malformed, or soft-deleted ID and verify that appropriate errors are returned. Test both boundary conditions, and validate permission checks for admin, reporter, and unrelated users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test abuse/violation report and extract its id to be used in the detail fetch test.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new abuse/violation report targeting a specific comment, review, or forum thread, ensuring only one target is assigned per report as enforced by the schema. Use a valid reporter and a legitimate existing target to check successful creation. Also attempt report creation with missing fields, invalid entity references, attempts to report non-existent content, and duplicate reporting by the same user on the same target. Confirm that error conditions, such as insufficient permissions and input validation failures, are handled with clear messages.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to serve as a valid abuse report target.

scenario.draft: Test updating an abuse/violation report's status, rationale, and resolver information. Start with creating a new abuse report, then as an admin or authorized actor, update its status (e.g., to closed or resolved) and verify the status, rationale, and resolver are updated correctly. Attempt unauthorized edits by a non-admin and confirm these are rejected. Ensure attempts to mutate immutable fields or change report targets are not permitted and return appropriate errors. Also check updating a report already marked as deleted or non-existent.

dependencies.purpose: Create an abuse/violation report to be updated in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion (logical removal) of an abuse/violation report by an authorized user (admin or reporter if business policy allows). After creating a report, delete it and verify it is no longer returned in listing queries or detail lookups, and its deleted_at timestamp is set. Attempt deletions with insufficient privileges, on already-deleted, or non-existent reports, and verify correct error codes and audit logging. Confirm deletion is logged for compliance and that no deletion occurs for protected or out-of-scope reports.

dependencies.purpose: Create an abuse/violation report that will be targeted for deletion in the test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of review snapshot records using multiple filter criteria such as review ID, customer ID, date ranges, and snapshot reasons. Ensure the search correctly applies filters, returns paginated results, and handles both matching and non-matching queries. Validate handling of too-wide/too-narrow pages, edge filters (e.g. boundary timestamps), and that total counts/reporting are accurate. Ensure permission enforcement (only accessible by administrator roles). Also check that requests with invalid filter schemas or unauthorized access yield appropriate error responses.

Test fetching a specific review snapshot record by its unique UUID. First, create a review and then generate a corresponding snapshot (see dependencies). Test success case by retrieving with a valid snapshot ID and confirming all fields match expectations. Then, request with a non-existent or deleted snapshot ID, and verify that a 404 Not Found or appropriate error is returned. Test role permissions to ensure only authorized users (administrators) can access review snapshot detail, and that unauthorized access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review to use as the basis for generating the snapshot.
Create a review snapshot for the newly created review.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new review snapshot record. First, create a review that can be snapshotted. Submit a valid snapshot creation request, ensuring all required fields are correctly supplied (review_id, content, rating, status, reason, etc.). Validate success and verify the returned snapshot record matches input values. Then, attempt to create a snapshot with missing required fields, invalid references (e.g., non-existent review_id), or violating business logic. Confirm that proper validation errors are returned and the snapshot is not created. Also verify that only administrators or permitted compliance actors can perform this operation, and unauthorized attempts are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review to allow snapshot creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing review snapshot. Begin by creating a review and generating a snapshot. Attempt a successful update by changing allowed fields (such as the snapshot reason or status) and verify the record is updated with the new values. Attempt to update a non-existent or deleted snapshot and verify an appropriate error is returned. Check that attempts to modify immutable fields (like the original review_id) are rejected. Lastly, ensure that permission enforcement prevents unauthorized actors from updating snapshots.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new review for snapshotting.
Create a review snapshot to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test logical deletion of a review snapshot. Create a review and a corresponding snapshot, then soft-delete the snapshot by its ID. Confirm the snapshot is marked deleted (if returned) and cannot be retrieved by normal means. Attempt to delete a snapshot that does not exist, has already been deleted, or for which the actor lacks permission; confirm appropriate errors are returned. Ensure soft deletes leave the historical audit trail intact and do not break downstream review history or compliance traces.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review record for snapshotting.
Create a snapshot to test deletion logic.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of favorite products for a customer. First, ensure the customer has at least a few favorite records (using the POST /ai_ecommerce/favorites endpoint for setup). Provide valid filter options such as customer_id, product_id, and favorite_tag_id, as well as pagination parameters (page, limit). Confirm the API returns only favorites matching the filters and the correct pagination metadata. Verify compliance with customer-level access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create favorite product records for a specific customer to ensure list results are meaningful. Must precede the listing test.

scenario.draft: Test listing favorite products when no records match the filters (e.g., using a non-existent customer_id or favorite_tag_id). Ensure the API returns an empty result set with appropriate pagination metadata. This validates correct empty list handling and search feature integrity.

Test listing favorites with various combinations of page, limit, and sorting parameters. Create enough favorites for the target customer to exercise multi-page result scenarios. Ensure the correct set of records is returned per page, and that sort direction and field are applied accurately. Validate accuracy in pagination metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Bulk-create enough favorite product records for the customer to test paging and sorting edge cases.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a favorite product by a valid ID. First, create a new favorite product entry and use its ID to request details. Validate the response matches the original creation data and that only authorized users (the owner or admin) can access the record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite record in order to obtain a valid ID for detail retrieval and to validate access control logic.

scenario.draft: Test accessing a favorite by an invalid or non-existent ID. Attempt retrieval using a random UUID that does not correspond to any favorite entry. Confirm the API returns a proper not found error and does not leak data.

Test the access control by attempting to retrieve a favorite record owned by another customer or with no valid session. Confirm the API rejects unauthorized access with a clear error code/message, protecting user privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new favorite record associated with a particular customer to simulate unauthorized access attempts by other actors.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new favorite product for a customer with valid data. Ensure POST body includes valid customer_id, product_id, and optional favorite_tag_id. Verify the API creates the favorite, returns correct data, and applies all validations. Retrieve the favorite afterward to confirm persistence.

Test handling of attempts to favorite the same product more than once by the same customer. First, create a favorite record for a given customer and product. Then, attempt to create a duplicate. Confirm the API returns a duplicate/uniqueness constraint error and does not allow multiple favorites for the same (customer, product) pair.

dependencies.purpose: Create the original favorite to set up duplication scenario.

scenario.draft: Test creation attempts using a non-existent customer_id or product_id. Attempt to create a favorite with invalid foreign references and verify the API rejects the request with a foreign key violation or not found error, protecting data integrity.

Test updating the favorite_tag_id for an existing favorite product. First, create a favorite and at least one favorite tag for the customer. Update the favorite to link a different tag and verify the new association is reflected. Confirm audit logging is performed and no data leakage occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite record which will be updated in this scenario.
Create one or more favorite tags for the owning customer to support tag assignment updates.

scenario.draft: Test updating a favorite to reference a non-existent favorite_tag_id or invalid product_id. Attempt the update and verify the API properly enforces referential integrity, returning a clear error for invalid update targets.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite product to update with an invalid tag or product reference.

scenario.draft: Test that only the owner or authorized admin can update a favorite record. Create a favorite associated with one customer, then attempt to update it using a different customer or unauthorized session. Confirm the API rejects the update with a permission or authorization error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite record owned by a test customer for permission checking.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a favorite product record by its owner. First, create a valid favorite record for a customer. The owner then issues a delete request for their own favorite. Confirm the record is removed and is not returned by subsequent list or get requests. Audit log should reflect the deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite record that will be deleted in this test.

scenario.draft: Test that only the favorite's owner or an admin can delete a favorite record. Attempt deletion of a record by a user who does not own the favorite, or with no authentication. Confirm the API returns a permission denied error and leaves the record intact.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite record belonging to a test customer for permission validation.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a favorite by a non-existent or already-deleted ID. Attempt to delete using a random UUID or by repeating a delete call. Confirm the API responds with not found or already deleted status and does not alter unrelated data.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of comments by providing various combinations of filters such as customer_id, related thread id, depth, and keyword in body. Confirm that only comments matching the search criteria are returned, that pagination metadata is accurate, and that soft-deleted comments are excluded unless specifically requested. Include edge cases like requesting a page size of zero or an offset beyond available results. Validate that unauthorized search attempts are properly restricted based on user role.

Test failure scenarios for comment search by providing malformed query parameters, such as invalid UUID formats, unsupported filter fields, or excessively large page sizes. Confirm that the API returns clear validation errors and does not process invalid requests, while not leaking any data. This ensures robust request validation and user guidance in case of misuse.

Test successfully retrieving the complete details of an existing, non-deleted comment by its valid UUID. Confirm that all expected atomic properties, author information, and related discussion context are returned, with sensitive or restricted information properly masked based on the requester’s privilege. This is a standard use case for rendering comment details in forums or review flows.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment so its ID can be used for detail retrieval, ensuring the comment exists in the system.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to fetch comment details with a UUID that does not correspond to any comment in the system. Confirm that a 404 error is returned and that no sensitive information is exposed. This scenario ensures safe error reporting and resilience against attempts to access invalid resources.

Test the case where a user attempts to access the details of a comment they are not permitted to view, such as a private or soft-deleted comment when the requester is not the owner or admin. Confirm that access is denied with an explicit error, maintaining privacy protection and compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment that is private or belongs to another user, preparing a scenario for permission validation.
Soft-delete the comment to simulate access to logically removed content.

scenario.draft: Test the successful creation of a new comment associated with a forum thread, using complete and valid request data. Validate that the response returns a complete comment object with all required fields populated, including timestamps and proper parent relationships. This scenario ensures the add-comment experience in forum or review flows works as intended.

Test creating a nested comment by providing a valid parent_id in the request. Confirm that depth, parent references, and hierarchical structure are correctly maintained in the returned comment entity. Validate restrictions to prevent circular or inconsistent nesting. This scenario enables threaded discussions and nested replies.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent comment before attempting nested comment creation.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario of attempting to create a comment with inconsistent or invalid context (e.g., referencing both a thread_id and an inquiry_id, or providing a non-existent target). Confirm the API returns a validation error, and no comment is created. This ensures foreign key and business rule integrity.

Test the security constraint that prohibits users from creating comments in contexts where they do not have permission (e.g., on someone else's private thread or review). Confirm that unauthorized attempts are rejected and properly logged.

Verify that the comment's author is able to update the body text or editable fields of their own comment using the PUT endpoint. Test that the returned comment reflects the new content, has an updated timestamp, and maintains the integrity of immutable properties. This enables standard comment editing flows.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as the test author to use as the update target.

scenario.draft: Test the security rule that prevents non-owners or users without permission from editing a comment. Attempt to update a comment as a different user and confirm the system rejects the operation with an error response, enforcing comment integrity and access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment under a different user context to test unauthorized updates.

scenario.draft: Test the failure scenario where a user attempts to update a comment that has been soft-deleted (deleted_at set) or locked for moderation reasons. Ensure the update operation is denied, and an explicit error is returned with no change to the comment's data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as the test user to prepare for update.
Soft-delete the test comment to simulate an update attempt on a logically removed/comment-locked entity.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a comment's owner successfully performs a soft deletion of their comment by ID. Confirm the deleted_at timestamp is set, the comment is hidden from standard listing endpoints, and remains available for audit or admin review. Validate that a 204 success or soft-delete confirmation response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as the owner before attempting deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that the API denies delete requests when performed by someone other than the comment’s owner or an admin. This ensures access controls by attempting deletion under a different user context and confirming an authorization error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a different user to simulate unauthorized delete attempts.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a comment using a UUID that does not match any comment record in the system. Confirm that a clear not found error is returned, and no side effects or misleading confirmation occurs. This tests safe handling of invalid deletion requests.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of product compliance rules. Verify that the endpoint returns only the records that match the filter criteria (e.g., partial rule name, date range). Confirm pagination metadata is present and correct, and that the requesting actor must have administrator privileges. Validate error handling when supplying invalid filter or pagination parameters. Edge case: ensure that requesting a page beyond results returns an empty item list but valid pagination structure.

Test that users who do not have the administrator role are denied access to the product compliance rule search endpoint. Attempt to retrieve rules as a non-admin and expect a forbidden or unauthorized response with a clear error message indicating insufficient privileges. This ensures RBAC is working as intended for compliance-sensitive endpoints.

Test retrieving the details of an existing product compliance rule by its unique UUID. Expect the full rule record to be returned with fields matching the stored rule. Validate correct handling when the rule exists and the requester has permission.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product compliance rule to ensure a known UUID exists for a successful fetch scenario.

scenario.draft: Test querying for a product compliance rule by a UUID that does not exist in the system. Expect a 404 Not Found error with a clear error message. This confirms the endpoint properly handles requests for nonexistent rules without leaking internal details.

Test creation of a new product compliance rule with all required and valid fields (such as a unique rule_name and appropriate description). Verify that the rule is created successfully and all fields are returned as expected. Validate business rules for uniqueness and field validation—ensure duplicate names or missing required fields trigger valid errors.

Test failure when creating a product compliance rule with a rule_name that already exists in the system. Expect a 409 Conflict or similar error indicating violation of unique constraints. This checks correct enforcement of uniqueness business logic for rule names.

dependencies.purpose: First create a product compliance rule to establish an existing rule_name for the duplicate test.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing product compliance rule's description or name. Ensure all business and validation rules are enforced (e.g., cannot create duplicate rule_name, description length constraints). Upon success, verify that the changes are reflected in the updated record. Ensure audit tracing is in effect if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product compliance rule to get a valid UUID for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating a product compliance rule using a nonexistent or malformed UUID. Expect a 404 Not Found or validation error, confirming the API does not allow updates to non-existent records and properly validates input.

Test updating an existing product compliance rule to have a rule_name already in use by another rule. Expect a 409 Conflict or appropriate error, ensuring that uniqueness is enforced during updates, not just creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first compliance rule to establish a taken rule_name.
Create a second rule with a different name that will be updated to match the first rule's name.

scenario.draft: Test soft deletion of a product compliance rule by its UUID. Expect the record to be marked as deleted or removed in a way that reflects system compliance policy (usually not hard-deleted). Confirm no longer accessible via detail endpoint, but may be listed in soft-deleted queries if supported. Validate permission checks for authorized actors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a compliance rule to get a valid UUID for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test deletion attempt on a product compliance rule using a UUID that does not correspond to any existing record. Confirm the API returns a 404 Not Found or appropriate error, and no deletion side effects occur.

Simulate an administrator retrieving a paginated and filtered list of return/cancellation requests. Test valid filtering by status, date range, customer, and order ID and confirm correct pagination mechanics and result set. Validate that only non-deleted requests are shown by default. Edge case: Filter on a combination that returns an empty result set. Check for permission error if an unauthorized user attempts to query.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test order to guarantee at least one eligible return request exists to filter.
Open a return request tied to the newly created order for filtering tests.

scenario.draft: Attempt to list return/cancellation requests with malformed, invalid, or excessive filter parameters (e.g., invalid status, impossible date range, or negative page/size values). Verify that the system rejects the request with clear error messages and does not return sensitive data. Coverage should include business validation on all filterable fields.

Fetch the details of a valid return/cancellation request by its UUID. Confirm that all expected fields are returned for active requests. Then, soft-delete the request using the DELETE endpoint and verify that subsequent fetches indicate its deleted status or return an appropriate error. Also, attempt to fetch a return request belonging to another customer as a regular user and confirm permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to tie to the new return request.
Create the return request whose details will be fetched.
Soft-delete the return request before attempting fetch of a deleted entity.

scenario.draft: Attempt to open a new return/cancellation request as a valid customer for a live order. Validate that all required business data are checked (order exists, within return window, not already returned, not duplicate). Cover edge cases: (a) supplying a non-existent order ID, (b) creating a request when a previous one exists for the same order, and (c) omitting required fields. Validate error responses for these cases. Also verify permissions: only the order owner or admin/support can open a request.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order as the customer to provide a legitimate context for the return request.

scenario.draft: Test updating the status or reason of an existing return/cancellation request. Verify allowed updates (e.g., pending to approved, adding more details). Attempt to update immutable or forbidden fields (such as changing the order_id or customer_id), and confirm the system blocks these with suitable error messages. Also attempt to update a finalized, rejected, or deleted request to confirm system enforcement of status-based business rules. Include update attempts both as the owner and as an unauthorized user.

dependencies.purpose: Set up an order for linkage to the return request.
Create a new return/cancellation request to be updated in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Perform soft-delete of a return/cancellation request as its owner/customer. Confirm that the record's deleted_at is set, that further retrieval now signals the deleted state, and that deleted records are not shown in normal listing. Attempt an invalid delete (already deleted, not found, or not owned by the actor) to observe permission and not-found error behaviors. Also check business logic: prevent deletion if the request is referenced in essential audits.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order and ensure it can be referenced by a return request.
Create a return request tied to the order for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of RBAC roles as an authorized administrator. Prepare sufficient roles in the database by creating multiple roles with varying names and descriptions. As an administrator, send a PATCH request with specific filter (e.g., role name contains a keyword), sorting, and pagination parameters. Validate that only roles matching the filters are returned and that the pagination metadata is accurate. Ensure sensitive roles cannot be retrieved by unauthorized actors. Also, test behavior when sending invalid filter or excessive page size—expect validation errors or resource limit error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple role records to ensure the list endpoint returns enough data for pagination and filters.

scenario.draft: Test that retrieving the list of RBAC roles is restricted to users with administrator privileges. Attempt to call the PATCH roles endpoint as a regular user or anonymous client, and verify that access is denied and a clear permission error is returned.

Test fetching the details of a specific RBAC role by a valid UUID as an administrator. First, create a role and extract its id. As an administrator, call GET /ai_ecommerce/roles/{id} and verify that the returned data matches the expected role details. Confirm all standard fields (id, name, description, attributes if present) are provided, and sensitive fields are not leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Create a role to obtain a valid role id for the get detail scenario.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when querying role details with an invalid UUID or a non-existent role id. Attempt GET /ai_ecommerce/roles/{id} with a random, non-existent UUID and another with a malformed UUID. Confirm the service returns appropriate 404 not found or validation error responses and does not leak sensitive system internals.

Test that only administrators are permitted to access single role detail records. Attempt to retrieve a RBAC role detail as a non-administrator and confirm that permission is denied with a clear error message.

Test that an administrator can successfully create a new RBAC role with a unique name. Send a POST request with valid role data (unique name, optional description). Expect a successful creation response, with the new role record including generated id and all provided metadata. Verify that the name is truly unique in the system and that audit logs (if applicable) are triggered.

Test creation of a role with a name that already exists in the system. First, create a role with a specific name. Attempt to create another role using the same name. System should reject the request with a uniqueness violation error, and no new record should be inserted.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial role with a specific name to set up the duplication scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that role creation is only available to administrators. Attempt to invoke the POST /ai_ecommerce/roles endpoint as a non-administrator and as an unauthenticated user. Both requests should be rejected with clear, permission-denied errors.

Test creation of a role with invalid input data. Provide a missing name, an empty string, or an excessively long name. Validate that the API returns appropriate validation errors, does not create the role, and response error messages describe the input problem.

Test successful update of a role's allowed fields (such as name or description) by administrator. Create a role, then update its name and/or description using PUT. Confirm changes are persisted and returned accurately. Ensure audit logs are correctly recorded.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new role to provide a valid id for update scenario.

scenario.draft: Test system behavior when attempting to update a role's name to one that is already in use by another role. Create two roles, then attempt to change the second role's name to match the first. The system must reject the update with an appropriate uniqueness constraint error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first role to establish the existing name.
Create the second role to be updated and tested for the duplication error.

scenario.draft: Test behavior when trying to update a role that does not exist. Attempt PUT on a random or deleted UUID. Confirm the API returns a not found error, and no records are changed.
Test that only administrators can update roles. Attempt to update a role as a non-admin or unauthenticated user, and ensure the API denies access and returns a permission error.

Test successful deletion (soft-delete) of a role by administrator when the role is not assigned to any user. Create a new role, then delete it. Confirm the deleted status/flag is set or the record is no longer retrievable via list endpoints. Check audit logs for operation traceability.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new role that is not assigned to any user, for safe deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that deleting a role currently assigned to a user is blocked. Create a role, assign it to a user (using whatever RBAC assignment endpoint is appropriate), and attempt to delete it. Expect a business logic error indicating the role is in use and cannot be deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a role for assignment to a user.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a non-existent role. Attempt DELETE with an invalid or random UUID and verify the API returns a clear not found or error response, and does not affect the roles table.
Test that only administrators can delete roles. Attempt to delete a role as a non-admin and as an unauthenticated actor, and confirm the action is blocked with a clear error.

Test that deleting a role currently assigned to a user is blocked. Create a role, assign it to a user (using the appropriate RBAC assignment endpoint), and attempt to delete it. Expect a business logic error indicating that the role is in use and cannot be deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a role for assignment to a user.

scenario.draft: Test that deleting a role currently assigned to a user is blocked. Create a role, assign it to a user (using the appropriate RBAC assignment endpoint), and attempt to delete it. Expect a business logic error indicating that the role is in use and cannot be deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a role for assignment to a user.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of trending product analytics. Scenario includes searching by product_id, stat_date, period, rank, or score. Validate that results are paginated, only accessible to administrator roles, and that filtering returns accurate and relevant trending products. Edge cases: query by non-existent product_id, extreme pagination values, and filters that yield no results. Verify errors for invalid filter parameters or unauthorized access.

Test retrieving the detail of a specific trending product analytics record by its unique ID as administrator. Ensure all expected analytic fields (stat_period, stat_date, trend_rank, scores) are present. Include negative cases: use a non-existent ID (expect 404), use a soft-deleted ID, and attempt access with insufficient privileges (non-admin user). Validate error response and field visibility for each scenario.

Test creating a new analytic record for trending products with valid and comprehensive analytics input—covering all required fields (product_id, stat_period, stat_date, trend_rank, stats/scores). Validate that only administrators may perform creation. Include failure scenarios: missing required fields, duplicate record insertion, invalid foreign key references (non-existent product_id), and invalid stat_period/stat_date. Validate error responses and audit creation in analytics context.

Test updating an existing trending product analytics record by its ID with a full replacement of all required fields. Validate that all updated properties are persisted accurately. Include negative cases: update with a non-existent ID (expect 404), violation of uniqueness (if stat_period/stat_date/product_id must be unique), invalid field types or out-of-range values, and attempts to update as a non-admin (expect forbidden error). Ensure all changes are correctly reflected in subsequent GET requests and that inappropriate updates are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a trending product record before attempting the update test, to ensure a known entity exists for modification.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a specific trending product analytics record by its unique ID as an administrator. Validate a successful delete returns a 204 or confirmation, and the record is no longer accessible via GET. Include negative cases: try deleting a non-existent ID (expect 404), attempt to delete as a non-admin (expect forbidden), and deleting an already-deleted record. Confirm audit trail and ensure deletion does not affect business data, only analytics cache or reporting.

dependencies.purpose: Create a trending product record to ensure an existing entity for the deletion scenario.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of permission entities. Scenario: An authorized admin user submits a PATCH request with filter parameters (such as permission name contains 'order', status is active) and pagination (page size 10, page 2). The response should contain the correct filtered permission records and proper pagination metadata. Verify that only the expected permissions matching the filter are returned and that the total count and page navigation work as expected.

Test failure when listing permissions with invalid or malformed filter parameters. Scenario: An admin user attempts to query with an invalid field or a page size exceeding limits. The service should return a clear error message explaining the filter violation or pagination constraint breach. No permissions data should be leaked and the error response must be structured for client handling.

Verify that users without admin or RBAC manager roles cannot retrieve the permissions list. Scenario: A non-admin user sends a PATCH request to /ai_ecommerce/permissions. The system must reject the request with a forbidden or unauthorized error, with no sensitive permission data returned.

Test successful retrieval of a single permission entity by ID. Scenario: An authorized admin fetches the detail of a permission that exists using its correct UUID. The API should return all normalized fields (name, description, creation timestamp, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission entity to ensure a known, valid ID is available before testing GET detail.

scenario.draft: Test error response when reading a permission by a non-existent or invalid UUID. Scenario: An admin user requests detail for a random UUID that does not match any permission. The response should be 404 Not Found, with a structured error message. No system information is leaked about non-existing IDs.

Test forbidden or unauthorized access to permission details. Scenario: A user without required privileges attempts to GET a permission detail by an existing or random ID. The system should reject the request with a clear unauthorized/forbidden message and no permission data in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission entity to obtain a valid permission ID for negative authorization testing.

scenario.draft: Test successful permission creation when all required and properly formatted fields are supplied. Scenario: An administrator submits a POST request to add a new permission with a unique name and description. The service should create the permission, enforce uniqueness, and return the full newly created entity, including its UUID and timestamps.

Test failure when attempting to create a permission with a name that already exists. Scenario: An admin first successfully creates a permission, then attempts to create another permission with the exact same name. The service should reject the second creation with a duplicate name error, and the response should explain the uniqueness violation clearly.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first permission with a name to subsequently test duplicate creation logic on a second request.

scenario.draft: Test validation error when required fields are omitted or incorrectly formatted. Scenario: An administrator submits a POST request lacking the required 'name' field or providing an empty string. The API should return a validation error, specifying the missing or incorrect property, and must not create any permission entry in the system.

Test failure when a non-administrator or unauthorized user attempts to create a permission. Scenario: Send a POST request to /ai_ecommerce/permissions as a user without elevated roles. The API must reject with a forbidden response, log the attempt, and not create any database entries.

Test successful update of a permission's description as an authorized admin. Scenario: First, create a permission; then, as the same admin, issue a PUT with a new valid description. Confirm that the returned permission object contains the updated description, all other fields remain consistent, and audit logging captures the change.

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission entity to obtain a valid target for subsequent update testing.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when setting a permission name to one already used by another permission entity. Scenario: Create two permission entities, then attempt to update the second's name to be identical to the first permission's name. The system must return a uniqueness/constraint error and not apply the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first permission with a unique name.
Create the second permission to update its name to the duplicate.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when updating a non-existent permission. Scenario: Send a PUT request using a random, non-matching UUID as the target permission. The API must return a 404 Not Found with clear messaging and not create or upsert an entry.

Verify forbidden or unauthorized error when a non-admin user submits a PUT update. Scenario: Attempt to update a permitted field on a real (or fake) permission record using a user with insufficient RBAC authority. The system should reject the update and log a security audit event.

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission to test access control during update as an invalid actor.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of a permission entity by its UUID. Scenario: As an administrator, create a permission and then delete it by calling DELETE /ai_ecommerce/permissions/{id}. The system should mark or remove the entry, log the deletion in the audit trail, and return confirmation of deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission entity for subsequent test of deletion by ID.

scenario.draft: Test proper API response when attempting to delete a permission by a non-existent or previously deleted UUID. Scenario: Issue DELETE with a random UUID or with a valid but now-deleted permission's ID. The API must return a 404 Not Found or appropriate no-op confirmation, with no side-effects or errors in audit logs.

Test forbidden/unauthorized behavior when a non-authorized user attempts to remove a permission entity. Scenario: Attempt deletion on an existing permission using insufficient privileges. The endpoint must refuse the action and respond with forbidden or unauthorized error. No permission data or status should be disclosed in the error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission entity for negative delete authorization testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of moderation actions. Simulate filtering by actor (administrator), action type, target entity (comment, review, or thread), and state (e.g., reversed, rationale, date window). Ensure that only administrators or authorized users can access the endpoint. Include boundary scenarios: empty filters (all actions), maximum page size, and attempting to use unsupported/invalid filter parameters. Validate error responses for malformed queries and permission violations. At least one scenario should ensure only permitted moderation actions are included in the result based on the requester permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create moderation actions with various actors, action types, and targets to set up necessary test data for search and filtering.
Provision administrators required for permission and actor-based filtering tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the full detail for a specific moderation action by ID. Set up a moderation action record with all fields (administrator, action_type, rationale, state, etc.) and ensure the test actor has permission (i.e., is an administrator). Validate that the response includes all schema-specified fields. Also check the response for deleted (soft-deleted) actions if allowed by role, and assert that access is adequately restricted for unauthorized roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action in the database whose detail will be fetched by this test.

scenario.draft: Test behavior when attempting to retrieve a moderation action by a non-existent or already-deleted ID. Ensure API returns 404 Not Found with a compliance-formatted error, and no unauthorized data is leaked. Also verify that unauthorized access to a real moderation action by an insufficient privilege role is blocked with a 403 error.

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete an existing moderation action before attempting read, or reference an ID that was never created.

scenario.draft: Verify successful creation of a new moderation action when the administrator provides all required fields (action_type, rationale, target entity reference, etc.). Check correct schema validation, actor legitimacy, and allowed action types (enums). Validate downstream logs/triggers if applicable. Upon success, details of the created action should be asserted, including ID, actor, and target references.

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator account to serve as the authorized actor performing the moderation action.
Create a target entity (e.g., a comment) to be referenced by the moderation action.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a moderation action while omitting a required field (such as action_type or rationale). Validate API returns a descriptive validation error indicating the missing property, and no moderation action is created. Check for a 400 Bad Request and proper error structure.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authorized administrator actor for the test context.
Create a valid moderation target (comment, thread, or review) to ensure other fields are valid for negative test focus.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a moderation action as a user without administrator permissions (e.g., a regular customer or seller). Validate API returns a 403 Forbidden error, and no moderation action is saved or visible in downstream queries. Ensure audit log records unauthorized attempts if required by compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer (non-admin) to simulate unauthorized access attempt.
Create a valid target entity for the moderation action attempt.

scenario.draft: Verify that a privileged administrator can successfully update mutable fields (e.g., rationale, reversal status, notes) of an existing moderation action. Ensure attempted updates to immutable fields (e.g., target, actor) are rejected with a clear error. Confirm that updates are persisted and all changes are audit-logged as required. The response must include all updated fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action with realistic values to serve as the target of the update operation.
Provide the admin account with privilege to perform updates.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action using a non-existent or deleted ID. Validate API returns 404 Not Found, with explicit error information. Ensure no unexpected side effects in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare the scenario by deleting a moderation action or referencing a truly non-existent ID.

scenario.draft: Try updating a moderation action as an actor who is not the owning administrator or does not have admin rights. Validate API returns 403 Forbidden, and the moderation action is unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action with a specific owner/admin.
Register a non-admin user who will attempt the forbidden update.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion of a moderation action by an authorized administrator. Confirm that after deletion, the moderation action's deleted_at is set and that the record remains for compliance, but is excluded from normal query results. Ensure the deletion is audit-logged. Also check that repeated deletion attempts are idempotent (return proper status with no side effects).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to serve as the deletion target.
Ensure the deleting user is an administrator with correct access.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation action as a non-admin or unauthorized user. Validate that API returns 403 Forbidden and the moderation action is unaltered. Check that unauthorized attempts may be audit-logged as required.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to attempt unauthorized deletion.
Create a regular user to simulate insufficient privilege.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation action ID that does not exist or is already deleted. Validate that the API returns 404 Not Found, and no error leak of underlying DB state occurs. Confirm idempotent handling for repeated deletes.

Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of personalization snapshots using valid filter criteria and pagination parameters. Ensure that the API returns only those snapshots matching the query parameters such as customer_id, snapshot_type, or date range, and that paging metadata (e.g., total count, current page) is accurate. This scenario should verify security boundaries, ensuring that only authorized data is returned to users with sufficient permissions. Handles both empty result sets for rare filter combos and successful calls with matching data.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one personalization snapshot record that matches the intended filter criteria to ensure a predictable response for positive filtering scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test the API's response to invalid or malformed query/filter objects (e.g., using wrong data types, unsupported filter keys, or conflicting pagination values) when listing personalization snapshots. Expect a 400 Bad Request response or a clearly documented error type, and verify the error object contains actionable remediation info. Business logic should reject excessive page sizes and improper filter combinations according to specification.

Test successful retrieval of a personalization snapshot's full detail by its valid UUID. First, create a personalization snapshot (with POST), then use its ID to query this endpoint. Ensure all expected fields are populated in the response. Validate that only authorized users (e.g., the owner or an admin) can access the record.

dependencies.purpose: Insert a known personalization snapshot to retrieve its UUID for the test.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to retrieve a snapshot by a non-existent UUID, a soft-deleted (already deleted) snapshot, or when requested by an unauthorized actor. Validate that correct error codes (404 for not found, 403 for unauthorized) and informative messages are returned, and that no sensitive data is leaked. Confirm access boundaries are strictly enforced.

Test the creation of a new personalization snapshot with required atomic fields (customer_id, type, timestamp, blob_uri, etc.). Provide a fully valid payload and verify a correctly formed snapshot is returned in the response. Confirm that the snapshot persists and is accessible by the owner or admin. Ensure business logic validates snapshot types and proper ownership. All successful creation events should be auditable.

Test system handling when attempting to create a snapshot with invalid input (e.g., missing required fields, unrecognized snapshot type, reference to non-existent customer ID, or submitting the same payload twice). Expect explicit error responses (400, 409, or 403), with details clarifying the failure cause. Ensure that no partial records are created and that transactional integrity is maintained.

Test updating allowed fields of an existing personalization snapshot by ID (e.g., changing blob_uri or type). First, create a snapshot, then attempt to update it via this endpoint. Validate business rules: immutable fields must remain unchanged, and only appropriate users (owner/admin) may update. Response should return the fully updated record. Audit trail should reflect the update action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a personalization snapshot to update.

scenario.draft: Test handling of update attempts with invalid field changes (e.g., trying to change immutable fields like customer_id or taken_at timestamp), invalid input format, or by unauthorized users. The API should reject such changes with a 400 or 403 error and provide an appropriate error message. Ensure the snapshot data remains unchanged after the failed update attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create a baseline personalization snapshot to serve as the attempted update target.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a personalization snapshot by a permitted actor (owner or admin). First, create a snapshot, then delete it and verify the deleted state (e.g., deleted_at set). Confirm follow-up GET attempts either result in not found or deleted status, and that non-authorized users cannot access the soft-deleted resource. Check audit/log trail for the deletion event.

dependencies.purpose: Insert a personalization snapshot to serve as the deletion target.

scenario.draft: Test error and security handling when attempting to delete a snapshot that does not exist, is already soft-deleted, or where the acting user lacks appropriate permission. Expect 404 or 403 error responses as per spec, with accurate diagnostics and no side effects or sensitive data exposure.

Test successfully retrieving a paginated and filtered list of order items for a user with proper permissions. The search includes valid filters such as order ID, SKU, or quantity and optional sorting and pagination. Verify the system returns only the order items belonging to the user's accessible orders. Ensure proper pagination metadata and that data returned matches the filter criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order record required to have related order items in the system for query.
Create a product in the catalog to ensure the SKU exists for the order item.

Create one or more order items linked to the order and SKU to appear in the filtered search results.

scenario.draft: Test searching for order items using a filter that does not match any items, such as a non-existent SKU or order ID. The system should return an empty result set with proper pagination metadata but no errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order so there is at least one valid order in the system; filter will intentionally not match this order.

scenario.draft: Test successfully fetching the details for a specific order item by its ID as an authorized user. Verify the response includes all expected data fields according to the schema and the user has permission to view the item.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order so that order items can be added and referenced.
Create a product in the catalog to ensure a valid product exists.
Create a SKU for the product, which will be referenced by the order item.
Add an order item to the existing order, which will be the subject of this test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving an order item by a non-existent ID. Verify the API returns a clear not found error response and does not leak information about other order items.

Test creating a new order item given valid order_id, sku_id, and quantity as an authorized user (admin or system). The operation should return the created item record. Validate that the order and SKU both exist and business rules for quantity are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to which the order item will be added.
Create a SKU so it can be referenced in the order item.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to create an order item with a non-existent SKU ID or order ID, expecting the API to return a referential integrity failure or not found error. The system must not create the order item and should provide a meaningful error message.
Test attempting to create an order item with an invalid quantity, such as a negative number or zero. The operation should be rejected and a validation error returned, with no order item created.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order for reference; SKU may or may not exist, but the focus is invalid quantity.
Create a SKU to be referenced; ensure invalid quantity is tested.

scenario.draft: Test successfully updating the quantity for an existing order item, providing a valid new quantity as an authorized user. The response should reflect the new quantity, and all business rules regarding inventory and quantity must be enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to enable the addition of an order item.
Ensure a valid SKU exists for the order item.
Create the order item to be updated in this test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an order item's quantity to an invalid value, such as zero or negative. Expect the API to return a clear validation error and not change the record.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order and add an order item to test update edge cases.
Provide a SKU needed for the order item to be edited.
Create a test order item to attempt invalid update on.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to update an order item by a non-existent ID. The API should return a not found error and not create or modify any items.
Attempt to delete an order item using a non-existent ID. The system should return a not found error and not affect any existing records.

Verify that the endpoint returns a paginated, filtered list of product tags based on various search criteria, including tag name and creation timestamp. Simulate multiple product tags existing in the database, and test pagination controls (page, size). Also cover edge cases of requesting an empty result set and boundary page numbers. Ensure no sensitive or non-public properties are exposed in the results. Only authorized roles should access this endpoint, but this is an open listing for tag administration workflows.

Check that requesting details for a valid existing product tag by its UUID returns all expected properties. Simulate having a product tag in place, and then request it by id. Ensure authorization is enforced if the tag is private or under restricted context. Confirm all relevant tag fields (name, creation date) are returned, and verify there are no extraneous or sensitive fields. The scenario should result in a normal tag detail response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product tag for use in the get-by-id scenario.

scenario.draft: Request a product tag by a random or non-existent UUID. The expected behavior is that the endpoint returns a clear 404 Not Found error, with an appropriate error message indicating the product tag does not exist. This tests system resilience against invalid lookups and proper error reporting under not found conditions.

Test happy path creation of a new product tag. Provide unique, valid tag name and properties (per schema requirements). After creation, verify the returned object contains the correct name, timestamps, and a unique identifier. Ensure that a duplicate tag name cannot be created for business rule enforcement. Ensure no sensitive data is exposed in create response beyond the expected schema fields.

Attempt to create two product tags with the same name. The first creation should succeed. The second attempt, with the same tag name, must return a validation or conflict error due to unique tag name requirements. This ensures business rule enforcement and appropriate error messaging for duplicates.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial product tag with a unique name to set up the uniqueness violation test for duplicate name.

scenario.draft: Update an existing product tag's name using a valid id and new tag name. Confirm that the update is successful and that the renamed tag is returned with new values in the response. Check that only allowed fields can be updated. Ensure audit trail or updated timestamp is properly set. Attempts to update to a name already used by another tag should be handled in a separate scenario.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial product tag to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an existing product tag's name to a name already taken by another tag. This update attempt must fail, and the system must return a conflict or validation error indicating duplicate tag names are not allowed. Test ensures enforcement of tag uniqueness on updates as well as creates.

dependencies.purpose: Create two product tags with different names for update scenarios.

scenario.draft: Delete an existing product tag by id. Ensure that the tag is removed and cannot be fetched afterward (should return not found if requested again). The test should verify proper permissions, referential integrity checks if tag is in use, and correct deletion confirmation. If tag is referenced by products, deletion should be blocked or handled gracefully (which may be tested separately if applicable).

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product tag to be deleted in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a non-existent product tag by providing a random UUID. The API should return a 404 Not Found error or another appropriate error message indicating no action was taken. This verifies robust error handling for deletion of non-existent resources.

Test paginated and filtered retrieval of order status logs. Verify the following: (1) As an authorized actor (e.g., admin, seller, or customer support), request order status logs using a variety of filters (by order ID, actor ID, status, or date window), including with no filters, single filter, and multiple filters. (2) Confirm correct paging: verify limiting, offsets, cursor mechanics, and that results match supplied parameters. (3) Ensure error is returned for malformed filter structures, invalid values (like wrong UUID format), or unauthorized access attempts. (4) Boundary test case: very large page sizes or requesting beyond available pages. (5) Confirm that only data the actor is permitted to see is returned (e.g., sellers see their own orders).

dependencies.purpose: Create an order that will have status changes (preparation for filtering test on logs by this order ID.)
Add a status log entry for the order to ensure there is a log to query and filter.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific order status log by its ID. (1) As an authorized actor, retrieve the log and validate that all returned fields match what was recorded. (2) Attempt to retrieve a status log as an unauthorized actor (not permitted for the given log) and expect a permission denied error. (3) Attempt to retrieve a non-existent log (invalid UUID) and expect a 404 Not Found error. (4) Confirm proper audit logging of each access attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order status log entry so that there is a valid log ID to fetch and to test permission handling.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a new order status log entry. (1) As an authorized actor, attempt to create a log with all required and valid fields: order ID, old status, new status, actor info, and timestamp. Confirm success and that record is persisted. (2) Attempt to create a status log referencing a non-existent order and verify that a validation error is returned. (3) Attempt to create a log with invalid enum values (invalid status code, wrong actor type) or invalid ID formats and verify that errors are returned. (4) Attempt to create a log as an unauthorized user and expect a 403 error. (5) Confirm that logs are immutable after creation and cannot be overwritten by re-POSTing the same data.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order to reference for a valid order status log creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating an order status log by its ID. (1) As an authorized user, attempt to update mutable fields of a fresh status log and confirm the change. (2) Try to update immutable fields (like ID or reference to another order) and verify that the system rejects these with proper validation errors. (3) Attempt to update a non-existent status log and verify that a 404 error is returned. (4) If log has become locked (by business workflow or age), confirm further edits are denied. (5) Attempt update as an unauthorized actor and expect a permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a status log record to ensure there is an updatable log for this test.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of an order status log. (1) As an authorized actor (e.g., administrator), delete a newly created status log and ensure it is marked deleted or removed as per business logic. (2) Attempt to delete a non-existent log and expect a 404 Not Found error. (3) Attempt deletion as an unauthorized or insufficiently privileged actor and confirm a permission error is returned. (4) Attempt to delete the same log twice and verify proper idempotent error (already deleted). (5) Confirm audit logging of the deletion action is present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new order status log so that there is a target for the deletion test.
